Rogue AI agents expose internet's frail foundation
market.summary: AI agents don't need to invent new ways to hack the internet to overwhelm its defenses. They just need to speed-run the ones humans already use. Why it matters: Agents are proving they can automate basic hacking techniques at a speed and scale that is turning the internet's long-standing security gaps into easy targets. Driving the news: OpenAI said late Thursday it had notified more than 100 organizations that its agents may have accessed their systems during pre-deployment testing. Researchers at Transluce and Corridor also found a new batch of incidents last week where AI agents targeted government websites, including those of the U.S. and Canada . AI companies and researchers are actively investigating tens of thousands of cases where frontier models went outside the bounds of their pre-deployment tests, Axios recently reported . Reality check: Agents in these rogue safety-testing scenarios are just emulating the hacking techniques — using stolen login credentials and exposed API keys while also bypassing bot detection — that human hackers have successfully used for decades. In many of the newly reported cases, agents were accessing publicly available databases and websites. "The hacks we saw weren't particularly sophisticated," Jack Cable, co-founder of Corridor and one of the authors of Transluce's report, told Axios. "They were quite limited, quite rudimentary." Yes, but: Some of the latest incidents happened while agents were performing mundane tasks unrelated to cybersecurity, suggesting agents don't always need to be told to hack before they start looking for security flaws. In one case, an agent tasked with finding Canadian divorce records from the early 1900s encountered roadblocks and tested for cybersecurity vulnerabilities as another way to retrieve the information. "The fact that it was happening at all is quite concerning," Cable said. Between the lines: The flood of AI-generated activity will still create new headaches for defenders. "None of these attacks are new," Michael Morgenstern, partner at DayBlink Consulting, told Axios. "But now a single person with AI can run them at scale." Tasks that once required a hacker to manually probe websites, hunt for exposed credentials or work around access restrictions can now be delegated to software that keeps trying on its own. Cable added that companies deploying agents, as well as the AI companies evaluating them, will need robust monitoring to catch agents behaving in unexpected ways. The big picture: The old cybersecurity playbook is still relevant. Closing exposed services, rotating leaked credentials and API keys, patching known vulnerabilities and limiting access still make many of these attacks harder. AI models are largely exploiting classes of vulnerabilities that defenders have "known about for decades" and already know how to prevent, Cable said. The bottom line: How companies defend their networks doesn't change just because the technology carrying out the attacks is new. Go deeper : Cybersecurity 101 still applies in the AI world

The complaint claims that AppLovin made false and misleading statements regarding its generative AI video creative feature, overstating AI model improvements and the benefits of its 'virtuous cycle' value proposition during the period from February 12, 2026 to August 5, 2026. Investors who purchased AppLovin securities during this period are encouraged to join the case, with a lead plaintiff deadline of November 16, 2026.

However, the report reveals substantial growth opportunities as 58% of Type 2 patients on GLP-1 medicines use CGM, and a majority are open to CGM when recommended alongside GLP-1 therapy. Competitors Abbott Laboratories and MiniMed are also expanding their CGM portfolios with innovative features and sensor technologies.

Additionally, CagriSema showed benefits beyond weight reduction, including reduced abdominal, liver, and pancreatic fat while maintaining bone health in diabetes patients.

NVO.title: Lilly vs. Novo: Inside the Milan EASD Showdown and the ETFs Poised to Win
NVO.summary: At the 2026 EASD conference in Milan, Eli Lilly and Novo Nordisk presented competing clinical data in the weight-loss drug market. Lilly's retatrutide showed 34.9% of patients lost at least 25% of body weight, while Novo countered with cardiovascular safety data for Ozempic. The GLP-1 market is expanding rapidly with over 27% of global adults eligible for these medications, attracting competition from Pfizer, Amgen, and Regeneron. SPRY.title: ARS PHARMACEUTICALS DEADLINE MONDAY: Bragar Eagel & Squire, P.C. Reminds ARS Pharmaceuticals Investors to Contact the Firm Before October 5th Seeking Lead Plaintiff Role

CVX.title: AI and Oil Shape Market Leadership in the First Nine Months of 2026

OKLO.title: GE Vernova's BWRX-300 Secures First US Construction Permit

The approval removes a major regulatory hurdle and establishes a foundation for standardized deployment across multiple projects in the U.S. and Canada. The company expects long-term revenue opportunities from fuel, maintenance, and services across the reactor lifecycle.

OKLO.title: Can OKLO Turn Used Nuclear Fuel Into a Scalable Business?

Meanwhile, competitors like Entergy and NextEra Energy are pursuing traditional nuclear growth strategies focused on generation capacity and fuel supply rather than recycling.

Average Hourly Earnings disappointed at +0.1% versus +0.3% expected, failing to keep pace with inflation. Despite weak employment data, stock futures surged as bond yields declined, with the Dow up +460 points, Nasdaq +375, and S&P 500 +71 points.

CpN.title: Jobs Market Stays Flat at +29K, Futures Love It
CpN.summary: The September BLS employment report showed only 29K new jobs created, significantly below the 84-90K estimate, with unemployment ticking up to 4.2%. Average hourly earnings disappointed at +0.1% versus +0.3% expected. Bond yields fell on the weaker data, and stock futures surged in pre-market trading.

CpN.title: Can Jefferies' Expanded SMBC Partnership Bolster Its Growth in Japan?
CpN.summary: Jefferies Financial Group is launching a Japan-based joint venture with Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation (SMBC) expected to begin operations in January 2027. SMBC has increased its equity stake in Jefferies to nearly 20%, becoming the largest shareholder. The JV will combine SMBC's domestic Japanese client relationships and equities capabilities with Jefferies' global investment banking network, targeting institutional equities and ECM opportunities. Early results show M&A and ECM market share for jointly covered sponsor clients increased more than fourfold since 2024.

CpN.title: Citigroup (C) Stock Declines While Market Improves: Some Information for Investors
CpN.summary: Citigroup stock declined 1.92% to $127.00 on October 1, 2026, underperforming the broader market which gained modestly. The company is expected to report earnings on October 13 with projected EPS of $2.7 (up 20.54% YoY) and revenue of $23.72 billion (up 7.39% YoY). Citigroup trades at a Forward P/E of 11.53, below its industry average of 13.03, and holds a Zacks Rank of #3 (Hold).

DAL.title: Fleet-Upgrade Efforts, Flying Agreements Aid SkyWest Amid Cost Pressures
DAL.summary: SkyWest expands its fleet with new E175 aircraft deliveries from major partners United, Delta, and American Airlines, while reducing debt and repurchasing shares. However, the company faces headwinds from rising labor, fuel, and maintenance costs that are outpacing revenue growth and pressuring earnings.

DAL.title: Here's Why Investors Should Give Delta Air Stock a Miss Currently
DAL.summary: Delta Air Lines (DAL) is facing significant challenges including downward earnings estimate revisions, elevated fuel costs (up 41% YoY), rising crew-related expenses, and weak industry performance. The airline carries a Zacks Rank #5 (Strong Sell) with shares underperforming the transportation sector over the past three months.

DAL.title: Wall Street Analysts See Delta (DAL) as a Buy: Should You Invest?
DAL.summary: The article examines the reliability of Wall Street analyst recommendations versus the Zacks Rank system using Delta Air Lines as a case study. While Delta has a strong buy-equivalent average brokerage recommendation (ABR) of 1.24, the Zacks Rank assigns it a Strong Sell (#5) rating due to declining earnings estimate revisions. The article argues that brokerage analysts exhibit positive bias due to vested interests, while the Zacks Rank, based on earnings estimate revisions, has a proven track record of predicting near-term stock price movements.

DAL.title: Delta Air Lines (DAL) Earnings Expected to Grow: Should You Buy?
DAL.summary: Delta Air Lines is expected to report Q3 2026 earnings of $1.96 per share (up 14.6% YoY) with revenues of $17.7 billion (up 6.2% YoY) on October 9. However, the stock carries a negative Earnings ESP of -2.81% and a Zacks Rank #5, making it unlikely to beat consensus estimates. While Delta has beaten estimates in 4 of the last 4 quarters, recent analyst revisions have turned bearish, suggesting challenging near-term stock performance.

XOM.title: Can Chevron's Growing LNG Network Power Its Next Growth Phase?
XOM.summary: Chevron is building a diversified natural gas strategy with LNG operations spanning Australia, Asia Pacific, the Eastern Mediterranean, and West Africa. The company's Australian assets (Gorgon and Wheatstone) supply 40% of Western Australia's domestic gas and 9.5M tons annually to Japan, while U.S. Gulf Coast capacity has reached 7M tons annually with volumes beginning in 2026. Industry peers ExxonMobil and Shell are similarly investing in LNG as a long-term growth avenue, with Shell targeting 4-5% annual LNG sales growth through 2030.

XOM.title: Is First Trust NASDAQ Oil & Gas ETF (FTXN) a Strong ETF Right Now?
XOM.summary: FTXN is a smart beta ETF providing exposure to US oil and gas companies with $970.56 million in assets. It tracks the Nasdaq US Smart Oil & Gas Index with a 0.60% expense ratio and 1.84% dividend yield. The fund returned 41.33% overall and 38.71% year-to-date as of October 2026, with top holdings including ConocoPhillips, Chevron, and ExxonMobil. However, cheaper alternatives like VDE (0.09% expense ratio) and XLE (0.08% expense ratio) offer lower-cost market-cap weighted energy exposure.

UWMC.title: Kaplan Fox Alerts GoDaddy Inc. (NYSE: GDDY) Investors to an Approaching Lead Plaintiff Deadline on October 20, 2026
UWMC.summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against GoDaddy Inc. for allegedly making false and misleading statements about customer growth strategy while implementing promotional discounts that materially harmed bookings growth. The company's stock declined over 14% on February 25, 2026, following disclosure of sharply decelerated bookings growth of only 5% in Q4 2025. The lead plaintiff deadline is October 20, 2026.

The move aims to give Helix greater focus and flexibility to accelerate growth and innovation in agentic AI ServiceOps solutions.

KKR.title: Can Lazard's Asset Management Growth Power Its 2030 Revenue Goal?
KKR.summary: Lazard (LAZ) reported $285 billion in AUM as of June 2026, up 15% year-over-year, with $7.4 billion in first-half net inflows—its strongest in nearly 20 years. The company is pursuing its goal of doubling firmwide revenue by 2030 through expansion of its Asset Management division, which now accounts for 42.1% of net revenue. Key growth drivers include the Lazard Advantage quantitative platform reaching $50 billion AUM, active ETF expansion, and strategic acquisitions including a controlling stake in Elaia Partners and the planned acquisition of Campbell Lutyens.

DXCM.title: DXCM Report Highlights CGM Growth Opportunity in Type 2 Diabetes Care
DXCM.summary: Dexcom released its 2026 State of Type 2 Report highlighting significant gaps in CGM awareness and reimbursement access, with 55% of Type 2 diabetes patients having limited knowledge of the technology. However, the report reveals substantial growth opportunities as 58% of Type 2 patients on GLP-1 medicines use CGM, and a majority are open to CGM when recommended alongside GLP-1 therapy. Competitors Abbott Laboratories and MiniMed are also expanding their CGM portfolios with innovative features and sensor technologies.

DXCM.title: ViCentra Presents Large-Scale Real-World Evidence Demonstrating Kaleido Insulin Patch Pump System Delivers Stable Glucose Control with Very Low Hypoglycemia
DXCM.summary: ViCentra announced real-world data from 3,918 adults showing its Kaleido insulin patch pump system achieved 72.2% median time in range with minimal hypoglycemia (0.21% time below 54 mg/dL) and low glycemic variability (28.7% coefficient of variation) across Germany, the Netherlands, and France. The system, integrated with Diabeloop's DBLG1 algorithm and Dexcom G6, demonstrated strong clinical performance in routine use with high user engagement.

YSS.title: YSS Investors Have Opportunity to Lead York Space Systems, Inc. Securities Fraud Lawsuit with SBS Law
YSS.summary: Schall, Brown & Schwartz LLP announced a class action securities fraud lawsuit against York Space Systems, Inc. (NYSE: YSS) for making false and misleading statements during its January 2026 IPO. The company allegedly failed to achieve fully functional mission and payload software before satellite launches, putting contracts with the SDA at risk. Investors who purchased shares between January 29, 2026 and May 11, 2026 are encouraged to participate, with a deadline of October 30, 2026.

CR.title: Taylor Devices, Inc. (TAYD) Q1 Earnings and Revenues Lag Estimates
CR.summary: Taylor Devices reported quarterly earnings of $0.14 per share, missing consensus estimates of $0.93 by 84.95%, and revenues of $7.3 million, missing estimates by 44.7%. The company has underperformed the S&P 500 year-to-date and received a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating, suggesting near-term performance in line with the market.

CR.title: Parker-Hannifin Benefits From Business Strength Amid Headwinds

The company completed the acquisition of Filtration Group and has a pending deal for CIRCOR's aerospace business. However, rising operating expenses, $6.77 billion in long-term debt, and $401 million in annual interest expenses pose challenges to profitability.

AGIO.title: Agios' Growth Story Hinges on Mitapivat's Commercial Expansion
AGIO.summary: Agios Pharmaceuticals' mitapivat-based drugs (Pyrukynd and Aqvesme) generated $44.7 million in Q2 2026 revenue, up 259% year-over-year, driven by early thalassemia adoption. However, the discontinuation of pipeline drug tebapivat and intensifying competition from Novo Nordisk's etavopivat in sickle cell disease have made the company heavily dependent on mitapivat's commercial success.

BMY.title: Autoimmune CAR T Safety Events Reshape Rheumatologist Sentiment, but Autologous CAR T Retains Lead, According to Spherix Global Insights
BMY.summary: Following trial pauses by Novartis and Bristol Myers Squibb due to safety concerns, rheumatologist confidence in autologous CAR T dropped significantly from 7.5 to 5.2 on a 10-point scale. Despite this, autologous CAR T retained its lead among immune reset modalities at 49% preference. Systemic sclerosis emerged as the clearest near-term opportunity, while delivery infrastructure and safety evidence are now critical differentiators for market adoption.

NVS.title: Europe Cancer Metabolism Based Therapeutics Market Forecast to 2035 by Modality, Route, Indication, and Therapy Sales | 25.3% CAGR Drives an $8.54 Billion Opportunity
NVS.summary: Europe's cancer metabolism-based therapeutics market is projected to grow from $1.12 billion in 2026 to $8.54 billion by 2035, representing a 25.3% CAGR. Growth is driven by Europe's high cancer burden, advances in molecular profiling, precision oncology adoption, and regulatory validation. Small molecules and oral administration routes dominate, with breast cancer and non-small cell lung cancer as leading indications. Key players include AstraZeneca, Bayer, Novartis, Roche, and Servier.

Q/C Technologies recently established a 4,800-square-foot integrated photonics laboratory in San Francisco.
